newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico will not swerve from market economy - Zedillo.
newsitem.headline: Mexico will not swerve from market economy - Zedillo.

text.p: President Ernesto Zedillo, meeting with officials from the Bank of Montreal and Mexican bank Bancomer, on Tuesday insisted Mexico would not swerve from its commitment to a market economy.
"Mexico will not take a single step back along the path towards building a solid market economy," an official communique quoted him as saying.

Some economists have been nervous that recent elections, in which Zedillo's long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) lost absolute control of the lower house of Congress for the first time in decades, might lead to some backsliding on economic reform.
But Zedillo said the election result would promote greater economic dynamism.

"This political stability will also be more favourable in generating a more dynamic and expansive economy that will allow us to further develop the levels of well-being our population merits," he was quoted as saying.
The president called the meeting with the two banks to discuss his plans for future investment in Mexico.
Bank of Montreal has an equity position in and an alliance with Grupo Financeiro Bancomer, one of Mexico's top two financial institutions.

"It is important for us to be able to count on the support of banks like that of Montreal, which through its association with Bancomer, is positioning itself as an active source of investment in Mexico," he said.
Bank of Montreal President Matthew Barret said Mexico had a close ally in Canada and that both countries needed to strengthen their ties. ((--Caroline Brothers, Mexico City newsroom +525 728 7902))
